item.title: Bird warns of legal risks to 60 seats
item.description: East Sepik Governor Allan Bird says electoral boundary errors affecting 60 parliamentary seats must be addressed urgently to avoid possible legal challenges ahead of the 2027 General Election. Govenor Bird raised the concerns in Parliament, citing information presented last week by Electoral Commissioner Professor Nicole Haley to the Special Parliamentary Committee on Elections, which he chairs.
item.content:encoded:
East Sepik Governor Allan Bird says electoral boundary errors affecting 60 parliamentary seats must be addressed urgently to avoid possible legal challenges ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Govenor Bird raised the concerns in Parliament, citing information presented last week by Electoral Commissioner Professor Nicole Haley to the Special Parliamentary Committee on Elections, which he chairs.

Governor Bird said the Electoral Commission could not correct the errors on its own under the law and might need to seek an interpretation of the Organic Law from the Supreme Court if a new Boundaries Commission was not established.

He warned that a court ruling against the boundaries could affect the legal standing of the electorates concerned.

Prime Minister James Marape acknowledged the boundary concerns but said the Government was considering how to address them through the required processes.

Mr Marape said the K150 million allocated through the supplementary budget, in addition to K50 million already provided, would support the Electoral Commission's work. He said the additional funding could include work to address electoral boundary issues if required.

item.title: PM says Boundaries Commission submission being processed
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape says a submission to establish the Electoral Boundaries Commission is being processed after East Sepik Governor Allan Bird raised concerns about electoral boundary errors ahead of the 2027 General Election. Bird, who chairs the Special Parliamentary Committee on Elections, questioned why a submission to establish the commission has reportedly remained with the NEC Secre
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape says a submission to establish the Electoral Boundaries Commission is being processed after East Sepik Governor Allan Bird raised concerns about electoral boundary errors ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Bird, who chairs the Special Parliamentary Committee on Elections, questioned why a submission to establish the commission has reportedly remained with the NEC Secretary for more than 12 months.

The Prime Minister in response said the Government was aware of the issue and was working through the necessary processes.

Marape said the Chief Secretary was handling the matter, and Electoral Commissioner Professor Nicole Haley is expected to provide a full briefing next Tuesday.

Mr Marape said the Government would consider the necessary steps to address boundary issues and support the Electoral Commission ahead of the 2027 elections.

item.title: New home biogas kit project launched in Hiri-Koiari
item.description: A project of home biogas kit that will produce natural gas for cooking was officially launched yesterday at the Lutheran Church in Karakadahu village in Hiri-Koiari, Central province. The home biogas kit project is expected to contribute to improved energy access, environmental sustainability, and agricultural productivity through the production of organic fertilizer for participating households a
item.content:encoded:
A project of home biogas kit that will produce natural gas for cooking was officially launched yesterday at the Lutheran Church in Karakadahu village in Hiri-Koiari, Central province.

The home biogas kit project is expected to contribute to improved energy access, environmental sustainability, and agricultural productivity through the production of organic fertilizer for participating households and communities, in producing natural gas for cooking.

Head of Mashav, an agency for international development corporation in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Israel, Ambassador Eynat Shlein, has recently launched the project, marking a new step towards sustainable energy solutions for communities in Karakadahu village.

Ambassador Shlein expressed that she was happy that the biogas technology has already been installed in Sogeri, adding that Israel views Papua New Guinea as a close friend and is committed to strengthening cooperation between the two countries.

"This project is one of 30 projects that will be launched in other provinces throughout PNG," she said.

The launch was attended by Ambassador Shlein and members of the Israeli delegation, including CNSU E3 representative Danny Kei, along with community leaders and project stakeholders.

Shlein also highlighted Papua New Guinea's potential for development and said Israel intends to support further initiatives, particularly in the area of human capacity building.

In addition, Rex Nou, first secretary to the member for Hiri-Koiari Keith Iduhu, said this project will help communities in their electorate, especially now with the El Niño issue.

“This new project will benefit us in the long run, especially with the El Niño currently that is affecting the country,” he said.

item.title: Kumul call up connects Biondi Odo to roots
item.description: Named at halfback to debut for the PNG Kumuls in this Saturday’s Rugby League World Cup opener against Lebanon is special for Bailey Biondi-Odo. The Kumul call-up from coach Jason Demetriou allows the 24-year old Queensland born play-maker an opportunity to connect with his Papua New Guinea roots.
item.content:encoded:
Named at halfback to debut for the PNG Kumuls in this Saturday’s Rugby League World Cup opener against Lebanon is special for Bailey Biondi-Odo.

The Kumul call-up from coach Jason Demetriou allows the 24-year old Queensland born play-maker an opportunity to connect with his Papua New Guinea roots.

Biondi Odo’s Kumul eligibility comes through a distinctive link through his grandfather, originally from Hula, Central Province.

“My Nana (Alu) and grand dad were born in PNG, they are from Hula in Central Province. My grand dad was adopted into the Torres Straits when he was really little,” he said.

“I don't know much, but I’m talking to all the Central boys in camp to learn more about my culture.”

The New Zealand Warriors-bound player recently concluded an impressive season with the Townsville Blackhawks in the Queensland Cup competition making 17 appearances with 13 tries and 19 try assists.

He joins fellow team mate Dudley Dotoi who has been named for another PNG Kumuls appearance.

Biondi-Odo will be partnering with London Broncos five-eighth Gairo Voro in the halves with support from Leigh Leopards hooker Edwin Ipape and speedster Morea Morea at fullback, making the spine.

“Training has been really great, the boys are starting to ramp up. We’ve got a good side and I’m looking forward to our first match,” he added.

The PNG Kumuls will be led by veteran captain Rhyse Martin who makes his third Rugby League World Cup appearance starting with the Lebanon side this weekend.

item.title: Banned sex enhancement products seized from five shops
item.description: Business houses in the country have been warned to comply with the country’s laws. This is after the Office of Censorship confiscated prohibited sex enhancement products from a major supermarket in Port Moresby, this week.
item.content:encoded:
Business houses in the country have been warned to comply with the country’s laws.

This is after the Office of Censorship confiscated prohibited sex enhancement products from a major supermarket in Port Moresby, this week.

The country’s Chief Censor Jim Abani revealed this in an interview with NBC News, today.

The Chief Censor Mr. Abani told this newsroom that despite ongoing awareness, businesses still fail to comply.

He did not disclose the name of the company however says the contraband items were confiscated from its five shops in Port Moresby.

This is the first offense by the company and it has been warned not to import and sell such items again.

He says though the country welcomes investments, employment opportunities and others, the laws of this country must be respected.

Going, forward the Censorship Office aims to improve its awareness efforts to businesses houses.

M Abani says penalty fees and charges for non-compliance have been reviewed and business that continue to breach the country’s laws will be slapped with fines as high as ten thousand Kina.

item.title: No boats, no aircraft to deliver 500 tonnes of relief to North Fly
item.description: The National Government is working on establishing a National Emergency Authority, to properly coordinate and work assisting disaster affected communities across the country. Minister for Disaster Services Dr. Billy Joseph said its [Authority paper] at its final stages and ready to be brought before cabinet.
item.content:encoded:
The National Government is working on establishing a National Emergency Authority, to properly coordinate and work assisting disaster affected communities across the country.

Minister for Disaster Services Dr. Billy Joseph said its [Authority paper] at its final stages and ready to be brought before cabinet.

“We will bring it to Parliament to make sure that we have a fully established National Emergency Authority in this country, just like in Australia, New Zealand, and even in the United States.”

Dr Joseph was responding to questions from North Fly MP, James Donald in Parliament on the lack of a national disaster response system and the possibility of a state of emergency declaration for this El Nino period.

“What is the National Government's long-term strategic plan to establish a permanent, fully funded and well-equipped National Disaster Response Unit with dedicated assets such as aircraft, buses and other emergency response equipment to ensure that Papua New Guinea can respond swiftly and effectively to disaster anywhere in the country?

Our people deserve a disaster response system that is prepared before a crisis strikes, not one that struggles to respond after lives and livelihoods have already been lost or affected,” Donald said.

Donald said PNG is a disaster prone country and despite this, the national response is largely reactive rather than proactive.

He gave the example of his province, where he is yet to distribute 500 tonnes of relief supplies to his people.

“In my province, fires are happening, rivers are drying up, ships cannot move and there are no supplies.

"The people of Western Province have no water to drink, they are looking for water to cook and the most affected are those in my district. We are running out of fuel because no ship is able to move these supplies. Our only means of survival is through air.

"I have been trying to supply 500 tonnes of relief supplies to my people. To my embarrassment, there is no barge, there is no aircraft, no nothing, because I can't bring in the supplies into the district, only through air. Fly River has dried up and it's very serious. This is a serious catastrophe,” Donald said.

At this stage, the National Government is not considering the declaration of a state of emergency to deal with the El Nino crisis experienced across the country.

item.title: K80 million Papua LNG forum cost questioned in Parliament
item.description: Parliament has been told that K80 million was spent hosting the recent Papua LNG Development Forum in Port Moresby. Finance Minister Thomas Opa confirmed that this was part of the K112 million ceiling, approved by the National Executive Council.
item.content:encoded:
Parliament has been told that K80 million was spent hosting the recent Papua LNG Development Forum in Port Moresby.

Finance Minister Thomas Opa confirmed that this was part of the K112 million ceiling, approved by the National Executive Council.

But Opposition Leader James Nomane questioned how the funds were disbursed, following reports that some landowners had missed out on allowances and accommodation

The recent Papua LNG development Forum, brought more than one thousand landowners from Gulf and Central Province , along with state agencies and stakeholders.

However, the cost of hosting the forum was under spotlight in parliament today.

Opposition Leader James Nomane questioned the allocation of the millions of kina to the forum at a time, when the country is facing the impacts of El nino.

He also raised concerns over reports that some landowners missed out on allowances, accommodation and meals.

Responding to the questions, Finance Minister Thomas Opa confirmed that of the K112 million approved by Cabinet, about K80 million had been spent on the meeting.

He said the forum had resulted in Gulf and Central Province agreeing for a 80 -20 benefit sharing arrangement.

However, the Opposition Leader demanded how the funds was disbursed, which received backing from East Sepik Governor seeking further clarification on how the K80 million was spent.

Minister Opa maintained that the forum was necessary to progress the Papua LNG project towards a Final Investment Decision.

He assured parliament that the National Petroleum Authority would provide a report on the outcome of the forum , including a funding breakup.

item.title: De Belin fired up for first World Cup
item.description: Papua New Guinea Kumuls Jack de Belin is prepared to make his Rugby League World Cup debut this Saturday against Lebanon at the Santos National Football Stadium. This marks his fourth year wearing the red black and gold.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea Kumuls Jack de Belin is prepared to make his Rugby League World Cup debut this Saturday against Lebanon at the Santos National Football Stadium.

This marks his fourth year wearing the red black and gold.

Just like all others that have come and gone in the past, including those in the present, the former New South Wales Blues prop is honored to represent his PNG Heritage.

The Kumul #314 is not new to the scene of playing in front of a passionate home crowd, however, this year marks a special phase as he runs out to play his first Rugby League World Cup.

The 35-year- old has a special connection to PNG through his grandmother with his dad born in East New Britain.

De Belin made his PNG Kumuls debut against Cook Islands in the 2023 edition of the Pacific Championships in Port Moresby.

“This is my fourth year (with the Kumuls), I joined just after the previous World Cup,” he said.

“It's been awesome, I've loved the footy team, the culture and the country. Being welcomed with open arms to play footy here is special.”

“I get to represent my dad and my family in this World Cup.”

Making 270 appearances in NRL, De Belin recently concluded his season with the Parramatta Eels after making 18 appearances since his move from St. George Illawarra Dragons (252 appearances).

Since coming into Kumuls camp, the main focus is remaining positive ahead of their opening fixture.

With less than two-days to go before their first fixture, De Belin said team preparations has been great having fair mixtures of the players who recently concluded their season in the NRL, Queensland Cup and the Super League competitions overseas.

“It's all about being positive and keeping up with the young boys, who are really proactive. The squad inside JD's (Jason Demetriou) pick is awesome.”

“There's a lot of local talent from Q-Cup and NRL including players from the Super League. We’ve got a wide variety and we’re ready to go.”

He is also joined by Parramatta Eels team mate Luca Moretti who is set to make his Kumuls debut.

Meanwhile the Lebanese Cedars will be led by West Tigers Prop Alex Twal during their round one clash in PNG.
